title: THE FACE THAT DID NOT KNOW

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant law in his hands, he was not aware that his face was radiant because he had spoken with the Lord. When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him." - Exod 34:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses came down glowing, and he had no idea. Everyone else could see it. He could not.

That is how genuine spiritual growth usually works. The people most changed by God are typically the least conscious of it. Those who announce their own spiritual depth are usually the ones we should worry about. Real transformation shows up on the face while the person is looking somewhere else — at God.

Time in God's presence marks us. Not with visible light, but with patience where we used to be sharp, with peace where we used to panic, with kindness that surprises people who knew us before.

We cannot manufacture this. Paul says we are being transformed into the image of Christ with ever-increasing glory as we behold Him (2 Cor 3:18). Beholding comes first; transformation follows. Stare at yourself and you will not change. Look at Christ and you will.

Note too that the people were afraid. Even reflected glory unsettles those who are not right with God. Faithfulness will sometimes create distance before it creates attraction — that is not always a sign you have done something wrong.

Spend time with Jesus. Let others notice what you cannot see.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has anyone noticed a change in you that you did not see yourself?
2. Are you more focused on appearing spiritual or on being with God?
3. What are you beholding most in your daily life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I want time with You to change me in ways I do not even notice. Turn my eyes to Christ. Amen.
